  "number": 144,
  "title": "feat(host-control): let Deck Apps call linked computers through built-in and custom plugins",
  "body": "A Deck App had no way to reach the computer next to it. This adds **Host Control**: link a computer once, and Deck Apps can call typed commands on it over the LAN. Commands come in plugins: built-ins every computer has, and custom ones an author writes, either with a Deck App or on their own. Plugins can also push events to Deck Apps the moment something happens on the computer. Closes #109, #110, #111; includes #145.

The design leaves room for later use cases without changing the contract: keyboard shortcuts, sensor gauges with controls, a Stream Deck-style grid, one Deck App driving several machines on different OSes, and a T3 Code dashboard. None of those are built here.

## How it works

- **Link once, then the Vita calls the companion** (ADR 0004, topology C).
  - VitaDeck starts one **LAN Listener** at boot (port 8787) for both Runtime Upload and links. The Shell's **Upload and link** row shows its URL and turns it off and on.
  - `vitadeck-host-companion link <vita-ip>` sends it the companion's id, name and URL; `vitadeck dev <vita-ip>` uses the same address. Nothing needs opening in the Shell first.
  - VitaDeck keeps up to 4 links, newest first, one per companion id.
  - Every companion `start` relinks the Vitas it linked (`relink: true`), so a new computer IP or port reaches them without `link`. VitaDeck updates only a link it still has; a computer forgotten in the Shell gets 404 `unknown_link` and the companion drops that Vita. A Vita that is off is retried every 30 s.
- **SDK:** `@vitadeck/sdk/host-control` is an additive subpath. `createHostClient(plugin, { hostId })` and `linkedHosts()` support several machines. Calls resolve to `{ ok: true, ...result }` or `{ ok: false, code, message }` and never reject.
- **Plugins:** a plugin is a typed registry (`defineHostPlugin(id, { name: command<Payload, Result>(guard) })`) that Deck Apps import, plus an implementation (`implementHostPlugin`) that the companion runs. TypeScript fails a missing or mistyped implementation, and the companion checks every payload.
  - **Built-in:** `core` (`capabilities`, `echo`, `events`, `notify`) and `systemStats` (CPU, memory, uptime) ship in every companion. Their registries come from the SDK.
  - **Custom:** `"hostPlugin": { "entry", "files"? }` in `vitadeck.config.json`. `vitadeck build` writes a `<slug>.vdplugin/` package (`manifest.json`, bundled `companion.mjs`, optional `files/`) and a `<slug>.vdplugin.zip`, like a Deck App's `.vdapp`.
    - With a Deck App: `vitadeck create my-app --host-plugin`.
    - Standalone: `vitadeck create lights --host-plugin-only` makes a project with no `entry`. Its `package.json` exports the registry, so any Deck App can depend on it (local path, git, or npm), with `@vitadeck/sdk` as a peer dependency.
- **Host Companion** (`@vitadeck/host-companion`, bin `vitadeck-host-companion`): one dependency-free bundle that stays `private` until a release.
  - `start`, `link`, `install <x.vdplugin.zip>`, `remove <id>`.
  - Installed plugins live in `~/.vitadeck/plugins/<id>.vdplugin`.
  - A running companion reloads them and any `--plugin ./dist` folder when they change, so an author's loop is `pnpm host` plus `vitadeck dev`.
  - `vitadeck` builds and `vitadeck-host-companion` runs. A single CLI would break `npx @vitadeck/sdk` and make users install the build toolchain just to run a server.
- **Events (computer → Vita), by long-polling:**
  - Plugins declare typed events (`defineHostPlugin(id, commands, { changed: event<Data>() })`) and emit them from a `start(emit)` lifecycle, which the companion runs while the plugin is loaded.
  - `core.events({ plugin, after })` answers at once, or holds the request until that plugin's next event, up to 25 s. The companion keeps 100 events per plugin.
  - `watchHostEvents(plugin, onEvent, { hostId })` keeps one wait open, so events arrive within a round trip and none fall between two waits.
  - `vitadeck-host-companion notify "Build done"` sends a `core` notice that any Deck App can watch; the demo shows it.
  - Native `fetch` now cancels pending requests when a Deck App stops, so a held wait never stalls a reload. WebSocket, SSE and a Vita listener were considered and rejected in ADR 0004.
- **Native:**
  - The upload server becomes the LAN Listener (`src/net/lan_listener.c`) with a `POST /link` route, and its request parsing moves to `src/net/http.c`.
  - `src/host_control/` adds the link store, `src/platform/lan_address_*` the shown address, and `nativeGetHostControlLinks()` exposes links to JS.
  - The Shell gains the **Upload and link** toggle (Runtime Upload used to start only from the Shell) and a Host Control screen that shows the `link` command and lists and forgets linked computers.
  - Because the listener now runs from boot, anyone on the LAN can upload a Deck App or add a link whenever VitaDeck runs, until credentials exist (ADR 0004).
- **Demo:** `js/examples/host-control` lists every linked computer with live CPU, and for the selected one shows its capabilities, gauges and an Echo round trip.

**Deviations from the issues:**
- The commands are plugins rather than a flat catalogue, so the wire request gains a `plugin` field.
- VitaDeck keeps several links, so the getter returns a JSON array, and the link payload carries a companion `id`.
- It ships as one PR instead of three, as asked; the commits still follow the slices.
- #111 has the Vita listen for links only while the Host Control screen is open. After testing, setup felt clunky, so links share the always-on LAN Listener with Runtime Upload.

ADR 0004, `CONTEXT.md` (new terms include **Host Control Plugin**, **Host Plugin Package** and **LAN Listener**), AGENTS.md and the READMEs are rewritten in place. Agent skills:
- New public `vitadeck-host-control`: companion, linking, plugin authoring and install, error codes.
- `vitadeck-deck-app-init`: learns `--host-plugin` and `--host-plugin-only`.
- `vitadeck-manual-testing`: gains a Host Control section.
- `vitadeck-vdapp-upload` and `vitadeck-build`: say where `.vdplugin.zip` goes and that `pnpm build` now builds the companion. Credentials are still deferred, so only read-only built-ins exist.

## Proof

- `scripts/agent-check.sh full` passed on 2a18bdfe (the head adds a JS-only review fix; fast tier passed on it): SDK tests 40/40, companion tests 37/37, lint and format, non-smoke CTest 18/18 including `host_control_link_harness`, the fetch-cancel case and the Shell's empty-library focus, Docker Linux smoke 2/2, and the Vita VPK build.
- New tests:
  - The SDK client, the companion and the C harness all replay the same contract fixtures in `tests/fixtures/host-control/`.
  - SDK CLI scaffolds:
    - `create --host-plugin`: typechecks, builds the package and zip, and its `greet` runs.
    - `create --host-plugin-only`: builds alone, and a separate Deck App imports its registry, typechecks and builds.
  - SDK CLI build:
    - `hostPlugin.files` is copied into the package.
    - A broken plugin build keeps the last good package.
    - Config and `dev` URL rules are enforced.
  - Companion CLI, end to end: zip `install` and `remove` against a running companion, `--plugin` folder reload, and a broken rebuild keeping the previous plugin.
  - Companion loader: rejects bad manifests and zips with several roots or `../` paths. A bundled CommonJS dependency and a package reading its own `files/` both work.
  - Events:
    - A held wait answers in under 1 s when the plugin emits, ignores other plugins, and starts over after a restart.
    - Stopped lifecycles' emits are dropped, an unloaded plugin answers `unknown_plugin`, `close` answers waits, and lifecycles start only after the port is bound.
    - CLI `notify` reaches a waiting `core.events`. `watchHostEvents` passes `next` as `after` and stops at once from a callback.
  - Native: `js_limits_harness` stops a Deck App while its fetch waits on a server that never answers. That took 15 s before the cancel fix and is under 3 s after.
- Manual passes in the macOS host window:
  - **Link and demo** ([screenshots](https://matemolnar8.github.io/vitadeck/site/host-control-screenshots/)): two companions linked, the demo's gauges and Echo, an offline companion, and forgetting a link.
  - **External user, from packed tarballs, with a globally installed companion** ([screenshots](https://matemolnar8.github.io/vitadeck/site/host-plugin-screenshots/)):
    - A `--host-plugin` app called its plugin, which read text from its packaged `files/`.
    - Editing a file and rebuilding reloaded live with no restart, and `remove` showed `unknown_plugin`.
    - A separate `deck` app depending on a standalone `lights` plugin (`npm install ../lights`) called it after `install lights.vdplugin.zip`.
    - `notify` showed in the demo within 0.4 s. The held `core.events` request had waited 12.6 s and answered in the same millisecond as `core.notify`; idle waits cycled at 25 s.

  - **LAN Listener** ([screenshots](https://matemolnar8.github.io/vitadeck/site/lan-listener-screenshots/)): with the Shell never opened, port 8787 was bound at startup, `link` and a `curl` upload both succeeded, and the demo showed the linked Mac. Turning **Upload and link** off made an upload fail with connection refused; turning it on restored it.

  - **Relink**: the companion started on a new port while VitaDeck was off, logged a retry, and relinked within 30 s of VitaDeck starting; the demo then polled the new port and refreshed its capabilities. After forgetting the computer in the Shell, a companion restart logged "forgot this computer", emptied its `vitas`, and the Vita stayed unlinked.

## How to test

From the repo root, on the host build. These steps use your real `~/.vitadeck/`.

1. Link and demo:
   ```sh
   pnpm --dir js install && cmake --preset default && ninja -C out run
   ```
   Pick **Host Control** in the Shell. In a second terminal, run `pnpm --dir js host-companion start` and accept the firewall prompt, then `pnpm --dir js host-companion link <your LAN IP>` (F1 shows the address under **Upload and link**). The demo shows live gauges. Try Echo, then run `pnpm --dir js host-companion notify "Hello"`; the notice line updates at once.
2. Act as an external author and user. In a second terminal:
   ```sh
   pnpm --dir js build && mkdir -p /tmp/vdp
   pnpm --dir js --filter @vitadeck/sdk --filter @vitadeck/host-companion pack --pack-destination /tmp/vdp
   npm i -g --prefix /tmp/vdp/global /tmp/vdp/vitadeck-sdk-0.5.0.tgz /tmp/vdp/vitadeck-host-companion-0.1.0.tgz
   export PATH=/tmp/vdp/global/bin:$PATH
   cd /tmp/vdp && vitadeck create lights --host-plugin && cd lights
   npm pkg set "dependencies.@vitadeck/sdk=file:../vitadeck-sdk-0.5.0.tgz" "devDependencies.@vitadeck/host-companion=file:../vitadeck-host-companion-0.1.0.tgz"
   npm install && npm run tsc && npm run host
   ```
   The `npm pkg set` line stands in for npm publishing. Stop the repo's companion from step 1 first, because both use port 8797.
3. In a third terminal (same `PATH`), from `/tmp/vdp/lights`, run `npx vitadeck dev <your LAN IP>`. Run **lights** in the Shell and press Enter on **Greet**. Edit the message in `host/companion.ts` and save; the companion prints `Reloaded plugins`, and Greet shows the new text.
4. User path: stop `npm run host`, then run `vitadeck-host-companion install dist/lights.vdplugin.zip && vitadeck-host-companion start`. Greet still works. `vitadeck-host-companion remove lights` makes it show `unknown_plugin`.
5. Optional, standalone: `vitadeck create lamp --host-plugin-only` in `/tmp/vdp`, then `npm pkg set` its SDK and companion the same way (the SDK goes under `devDependencies` and `peerDependencies`). Build it, `install dist/lamp.vdplugin.zip`, and in a Deck App run `npm install ../lamp` and `import { hostPlugin } from "lamp"`.
6. On the Vita: `pnpm --dir js build`, then `full` builds the VPK. Not tested on hardware.

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Always-on LAN upload/link without credentials expands attack surface; changes span native HTTP, Shell UX, and a new author-facing SDK/companion contract.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **Host Control** so Deck Apps can run typed commands on linked Mac/Windows/Linux machines via **`vitadeck-host-companion`**, with built-in `core` / `systemStats` plugins and author-defined **`.vdplugin`** packages from `vitadeck create --host-plugin` or `--host-plugin-only`.
> 
> **Networking and Shell:** Runtime Upload and **`POST /link`** now share one **LAN Listener** (`src/net/lan_listener.c`, `src/net/http.c`) that starts with VitaDeck (port 8787). The Shell adds **Upload and link** (toggle) and **Host Control** (list/forget links, up to 4). Native code stores links and exposes **`nativeGetHostControlLinks()`**; **`@vitadeck/sdk/host-control`** provides `createHostClient`, `linkedHosts`, and long-poll **`watchHostEvents`**. Events use companion-side waits (25s) plus fetch cancel on Deck App stop.
> 
> **Companion and build:** New **`@vitadeck/host-companion`** CLI (`start`, `link`, `install`, `notify`, hot reload). **`pnpm build`** bundles it; agent-check **`fast`** tier adds companion tests. Docs, ADR 0004, CONTEXT.md, skills, and a **`host-control`** example Deck App are updated for the new lifecycle (no “open Upload first”).
>
